traveler: Jheronimus van Aken, called Hieronymus Bosch
title: The Painter Who Stayed: Six Decades on One Market Square, and Five Centuries of Travelling Panels
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Aachen, the name the family carried west
stops.date_confidence: no date whatever. The Aachen origin is inferred from the surname alone; the year here is a nominal placeholder for a move no document records
stops.campa: The van Akens are named for Aachen, Charlemagne's city, and the name is the whole of the evidence. No document places a single one of them inside its walls, no year marks the move west into Brabant, and no property or guild entry survives on the German side. Aachen lies about a hundred miles east of 's-Hertogenbosch, across the Meuse and outside the duchy. The painter who inherits the name will not use it on his panels. He signs them Jheronimus Bosch, after the duke's wood, the town where his grandfather worked.
suggested_refs: The toponymic surname van Aken, 'from Aachen', as the family's only trace of its origin
sources: Genealogical tradition cited in Koldeweij, Vandenbroeck and Vermet, Hieronymus Bosch: The Complete Paintings and Drawings (2001)

stops.name: Nijmegen, the forefathers on the Waal
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The Nijmegen link belongs to unnamed forefathers, not to the documented grandfather Jan van Aken; no year attaches to it
stops.campa: The family's forefathers are placed at Nijmegen by genealogists working backward from the 's-Hertogenbosch registers. Which generation is meant, nobody can say; the archives name the grandfather Jan van Aken only once he is already in Brabant. Painters in these decades move between the towns of Guelders and Brabant as work and guild rules allow, taking a commission in one river town and citizenship in another. Nijmegen sits on the Waal, the southern arm of the Rhine, on the road that runs west and south into Brabant.
suggested_refs: Genealogical reconstruction of the van Aken line in Koldeweij et al. (2001)

stops.name: Markt, 's-Hertogenbosch: the grandfather enters the record
stops.date_confidence: attested; the municipal record of 1430 is the family's first firm appearance
stops.campa: Jan van Aken, painter, enters the municipal records of 's-Hertogenbosch for the first time. What he painted is unknown; no panel survives under his name. He founds in this town a trade the family will keep for three generations. The house on the Markt is a working shop, with patterns and pigments in it, long before it is anybody's birthplace. He dies in 1454, and his sons take up the brushes after him, among them Anthonius, who serves the Illustrious Brotherhood of Our Lady as its artistic adviser.
suggested_refs: Municipal records of 's-Hertogenbosch, 1430 and 1454, naming Jan van Aken
sources: Municipal 's-Hertogenbosch archives, cited in Koldeweij et al. (2001)

stops.name: Markt, 's-Hertogenbosch: the birth in the grandfather's house
stops.date_confidence: estimated. No baptismal entry and no birth notice survive; the year is worked backward from a portrait drawing made shortly before his death in 1516, and sources hedge it as undetermined
stops.campa: A son is born to Anthonius van Aken in the grandfather's house and is christened Jheronimus. No baptismal entry survives and no notice of the day; the year is reached backward from a portrait drawing made of him not long before his death, whose sitter looks to be a man of sixty-six. He will be the fourth generation of painters in one family and the only one anybody remembers. Around him the shop runs on the ordinary business of the trade: gilding, altar frames, the polychroming of carved wood, banners for processions.
suggested_refs: The Recueil d'Arras portrait drawing, the source of the estimated birth year
sources: Wikipedia, 'Hieronymus Bosch' (birth date 'has not been determined with certainty')

stops.name: Sint-Janskathedraal, 's-Hertogenbosch: the church that employs the family
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The baptism is very likely but unproven; no parish register of the 1450s survives to prove it, and the year is nominal
stops.campa: The collegiate church of Saint John rises over the town in a Brabantine Gothic that takes a century and a half to finish, and the van Akens work on its fabric: painted decoration, the maintenance of what the masons leave bare. Jheronimus is very likely carried here to be baptized, though no register proves it. The building is the family's employer before it is the boy's parish. Inside it the Illustrious Brotherhood of Our Lady keeps a chapel and a wooden image of the Virgin that draws pilgrims from across the Low Countries.
suggested_refs: Sint-Janskathedraal, 's-Hertogenbosch, and the fabric accounts naming van Aken painters
sources: Wikipedia, 'Hieronymus Bosch' and 'Brotherhood of Our Lady'

stops.name: Grote Markt, 's-Hertogenbosch: the fire of 1463
stops.date_confidence: the fire and the figure of some four thousand houses are attested in the municipal chronicle; that Bosch witnessed it is conjecture, hedged in Dutch sources as 'mogelijk'
stops.campa: Fire takes the town. Some four thousand houses burn, the greater part of 's-Hertogenbosch, and the flames run through the streets around the marketplace where the van Akens live and work. Jheronimus is about thirteen. Scholars who look at the burning cities behind his hells, the black towns lit from within, have wanted the fire and the paintings joined, and nothing in the archive joins them. Whether the boy stood and watched, the Dutch chroniclers say only mogelijk, possibly.
suggested_refs: Municipal chronicle of 's-Hertogenbosch for the fire of 1463

stops.name: 's-Hertogenbosch, the first entry naming him
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day in the municipal records
stops.campa: Jheronimus van Aken is named for the first time in the municipal records of 's-Hertogenbosch, listed alongside two brothers and a sister. He is roughly twenty-four. The entry says nothing of painting and nothing of him personally; it is an administrative line in which a family appears as a family. Nothing written earlier can be shown to be about him rather than about his father or his grandfather. From this date the town's registers carry him for forty-two years, in tax rolls, in property transfers, and in the account books of a confraternity.
suggested_refs: The municipal entry of 5 April 1474, first document naming Bosch

stops.name: Markt, 's-Hertogenbosch: the father dies and the shop changes hands
stops.date_confidence: approximate. Sources give only 'died c. 1478'; the inheritance of the workshop is inferred from ordinary practice, not from a probate document anyone has produced
stops.campa: Anthonius van Aken dies, in or near this year, and the sources give no better date. He had served the Illustrious Brotherhood of Our Lady as its artistic adviser, and the shop on the Markt passes to his sons. Within a few years Jheronimus is signing panels as a master, using the town's name and not the family's. What exactly he took over from his father, tools, patterns, the standing custom of the confraternity, no probate document says; it is what a workshop was made of, and what such a death normally handed on.
suggested_refs: The van Aken workshop on the Markt, inherited c. 1478

stops.name: Inden Salvatoer, the Markt: the marriage
stops.date_confidence: not a documented year. The records allow only 'sometime between 1479 and 1481'
stops.campa: Bosch marries Aleid Goyaerts van den Meervenne, a few years his senior and out of a wealthy house. The exact year is not fixed; the records allow 1479, 1480, or 1481, and no marriage contract has been printed. Her property comes with her, among it the stone house on the Markt called Inden Salvatoer, one of the best addresses in the town, and a house and land at Oirschot. The house stands on the same market square as the family shop. From here on he is not obliged to take every commission offered.
suggested_refs: The house Inden Salvatoer on the Markt, brought to Bosch by his marriage

stops.name: Oirschot, the wife's inherited land
stops.date_confidence: the move is stated flatly in the sources; the year is nominal, following the marriage, and no document dates the removal itself
stops.campa: South of 's-Hertogenbosch lies Oirschot, where Aleid has inherited a house and land from her family, and the couple moves there. No document places him at work in the village, no panel is tied to it, and the specific estate named in some accounts cannot be confirmed. Twenty miles is the greatest distance from the Markt that any record puts him, and it does not take him out of Brabant. Oirschot is farms, a church, and the road back north to the town where he was born and where he will be buried.
suggested_refs: Aleid Goyaerts van den Meervenne's inherited property at Oirschot
sources: Wikipedia, 'Hieronymus Bosch' ('the couple moved to the nearby town of Oirschot')

stops.name: Sint-Janskathedraal, 's-Hertogenbosch: sworn into the Brotherhood
stops.date_confidence: given in the sources as 1486/7; the three lenses of this research gave 1486, 1487 and 1486/88, and the '88' variant has no source behind it
stops.campa: Bosch is sworn into the Illustrious Brotherhood of Our Lady: some forty sworn members around a wooden image of the Virgin in Saint John's, with thousands of outer members scattered across Europe. Founded in 1318, it draws the town's clergy, magistrates, and richest families. Its sworn men are called swan brethren, for the swans each donates to the annual banquet. The account books survive, and almost everything anyone knows about his working life is an entry in them.
suggested_refs: The account books of the Illustre Lieve Vrouwe Broederschap, 's-Hertogenbosch
sources: Wikipedia, 'Hieronymus Bosch' and 'Brotherhood of Our Lady'
Illustrious Brotherhood of Our Lady account books, 's-Hertogenbosch archives

stops.name: The Brotherhood chapel, Sint-Jan: a retable ordered and lost
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The commission is cited from the Brotherhood account books, which were not directly reachable in this research; the range c. 1488-93 rests on that citation alone
stops.campa: The Brotherhood commissions from its new member a large carved and painted retable for its own chapel. The account books register the work; the object itself is gone, replaced later by another altarpiece, and no fragment has been traced to it with confidence. What Bosch designed for the confraternity that shaped his father's career and his own is therefore known as a line of expenditure and nothing else. The dates usually given, roughly 1488 to 1493, come out of the same books.
suggested_refs: Illustrious Brotherhood of Our Lady account books recording the retable commission
sources: Illustrious Brotherhood of Our Lady account books, 's-Hertogenbosch (cited, not directly consulted)

stops.name: Markt workshop, 's-Hertogenbosch: the Adoration of the Magi
stops.date_confidence: c. 1494, a scholarly estimate; Bosch dated no painting, and the donor identification that anchors the date is contested
stops.campa: Bosch paints the Adoration of the Magi as a triptych. Inside, flanking the kings at the stable, kneel a donor and his wife, identified on heraldic grounds as the Antwerp couple Peeter Scheyfve and Agneese de Gramme; specialists still argue the point. He puts no year on the panel, as he puts a year on nothing, so what is known about when he worked comes from tree rings in the oak and from the cut of the donors' clothes. Closed, the wings show a grisaille Mass of Saint Gregory, grey as carved stone.
suggested_refs: The Adoration of the Magi triptych, Museo del Prado, with its grisaille exterior
sources: Koldeweij et al. (2001), on the contested donor identification

stops.name: Markt workshop, 's-Hertogenbosch: The Garden of Earthly Delights
stops.date_confidence: estimate only. Bosch dated no paintings; the triptych is placed in a transitional stretch between his middle and late periods, and no contract or payment record for it has ever surfaced
stops.campa: He paints the three panels later called The Garden of Earthly Delights, and dates nothing. Closed, the wings show a grey sphere, the world on the third day, water and land and no people yet, with a line of the psalter written above it. Opened, they stand nearly four metres across and run from Eden to a garden of naked bathers, outsized fruit and birds, and then to a hell built out of musical instruments. No contract, letter, or entry in any register names who asked him for it.
stops.quote: Ipse dixit, et facta sunt: ipse mandavit, et creata sunt
stops.quote_source: Vulgate Psalm 33:9 (32:9), painted in grisaille on the closed outer wings of The Garden of Earthly Delights, Museo del Prado
suggested_refs: The closed exterior of The Garden of Earthly Delights, the Third Day of Creation in grisaille

stops.name: Brussels, the Habsburg court orders a Last Judgement
stops.date_confidence: the 1504 commission is attested in the Habsburg-Burgundian court accounts; the specific day '9 September' given in some accounts could not be verified here
stops.campa: The Habsburg court accounts record a payment: Philip the Handsome, ruler of the Netherlands and heir to the Emperor Maximilian, orders a large Last Judgement from Jheronimus van Aeken, painter, of 's-Hertogenbosch. The panel does not survive, or has not been identified. A Last Judgement triptych now in Vienna is sometimes proposed for it, on the strength of a donor face on an outer wing that resembles Philip, and the proposal has never been settled. The document is a Brussels document. Whether Bosch himself came to Brussels for it, nothing says.
suggested_refs: Habsburg-Burgundian court accounts of 1504 recording the Last Judgement commission

stops.name: Markt workshop, 's-Hertogenbosch: the Temptation of Saint Anthony
stops.date_confidence: contested. This research produced 1495-1500 in one lens and 1505 in another; the honest range is c. 1500-1510, within the late production, and the panel cannot be dated more closely
stops.campa: He paints the Temptation of Saint Anthony as a triptych: the hermit of the Egyptian desert set down in a burning Netherlandish landscape, besieged by hybrids, his pig and his tau cross beside him. The pig is not invention. The Hospital Brothers of Saint Anthony kept pigs that foraged the streets under bell collars, a privilege of an order that ran hospitals for sufferers of ergotism, and the animal followed the saint into every picture made of him. Bosch paints it where every picture of that saint puts it, at his feet.
suggested_refs: The Temptation of Saint Anthony triptych, Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga, Lisbon
sources: san_antonio_abad.journey.json, on the tau cross and the Antonine pigs

stops.name: 's-Hertogenbosch, no record of any journey
stops.date_confidence: an argument from silence covering c. 1480-1516, not a positive finding; the nominal date stands for the whole span
stops.campa: No surviving document places Bosch outside the Duchy of Brabant. There is no record of a journey to Italy, no guild entry in another city, no letter written from a road. The absence is not proof; men travel without leaving paper, and archives burn, as this town's very nearly did in 1463. His town is the fourth city of Brabant, on trade roads that run to Antwerp and to the Rhine, and men leave it in every direction all his life. What can be said is narrower than it sounds. The registers that name him for forty years name him at 's-Hertogenbosch and at Oirschot, and they stop there.
suggested_refs: 's-Hertogenbosch civic and tax archives, summarized in Koldeweij et al. (2001)

stops.name: Markt workshop, 's-Hertogenbosch: The Haywain
stops.date_confidence: dendrochronological, around 1516, in the last years of his life
stops.campa: He paints The Haywain: a cart of hay dragged toward hell while men claw handfuls out of it, kings and a pope riding behind, a pair of lovers on top of the load. Tree rings in the oak put the panel in the last years of his life, around 1516. The subject is a Netherlandish proverb made visible: the world is a haystack, and each man grabs what he can. Anyone in the market square below the workshop could have said that sentence. Closed, the outer wings show a wayfarer on a road.
suggested_refs: The Haywain Triptych, Museo del Prado, dated by dendrochronology

segments.name: The Requiem and the First Witnesses

stops.name: Sint-Janskathedraal, 's-Hertogenbosch: the requiem in the ledger
stops.date_confidence: attested as the date of the recorded funeral and burial, not of death. No death date survives; he died some unknown number of days earlier
stops.campa: On the ninth of August the Brotherhood of Our Lady enters a solemn requiem for its sworn brother Jheronimus in its account book. That entry is the anchor of his death, and it is a burial date, not a death date; he died some days before it, nobody knows how many. He is buried in or near Saint John's, close to the Brotherhood's chapel. No stone marks the place, no tomb was raised, and the spot inside the building is lost. The account book records the mass and what it cost.
suggested_refs: The Brotherhood of Our Lady account book entry recording the requiem of 9 August 1516
sources: Illustrious Brotherhood of Our Lady account books, cited in Silver (2006) and Gibson (1973)

stops.name: Colmar, the same saint finished the same year
stops.date_confidence: attested; the Isenheim Altarpiece is dated 1512-1516. The pin is Colmar, where the altarpiece hangs today, not Issenheim, where it was installed
stops.campa: In the same year, at Issenheim in Alsace, Matthias Grunewald finishes an altarpiece for the monastery hospital of the Antonines, whose brothers treat ergotism, the burning sickness called Saint Anthony's fire. One wing shows the hermit thrown down and torn at by demons: the identical subject Bosch painted in 's-Hertogenbosch, worked by a man who so far as anyone knows never saw a Bosch panel. No contact between the two painters is documented. The altarpiece hangs today at Colmar, a few miles up the road from the ward it was made for.
suggested_refs: The Isenheim Altarpiece, Musee Unterlinden, Colmar, and its Temptation of Saint Anthony wing

stops.name: Hof van Savoye, Mechelen: a Habsburg inventory
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The inventory of Margaret of Austria at Mechelen is cited for 1516 but was not directly consulted in this research
stops.campa: An inventory taken at the court of Margaret of Austria, regent of the Habsburg Netherlands, in her residence at Mechelen, lists a Temptation of Saint Anthony by Bosch. If the dating holds, the painter is dead or dying while a Habsburg regent already keeps his work among her pictures. She governs the Netherlands from this house for her nephew, the boy who will be Charles V. The entry is thin and has been read more than one way. Which picture hung in her rooms, and whether it was the triptych now in Lisbon or another version of the subject, the inventory does not settle.
suggested_refs: The 1516 inventory of Margaret of Austria at the Hof van Savoye, Mechelen
sources: Inventory of Margaret of Austria, Mechelen, 1516 (cited, not directly consulted)

stops.name: Nassau Palace, Brussels: the first eyewitness
stops.date_confidence: attested; de Beatis kept the diary during the 1517 journey
stops.campa: Antonio de Beatis, Italian canon and secretary to Cardinal Luigi d'Aragona, travels the Low Countries with his master and is shown through the Nassau family's palace in Brussels. He writes down what is on the panels there: seas, skies, woods, meadows, people crawling out of a shell. He is admiring and puzzled, offers no reading of them, and shows no worry about not having one. This is the first description anyone made of The Garden of Earthly Delights, written one year after the painter's death.
stops.quote: there are some panels on which bizarre things have been painted. They represent seas, skies, woods, meadows, and many other things, such as people crawling out of a shell, others that bring forth birds, men and women, whites and blacks doing various activities and poses.
stops.quote_source: Antonio de Beatis, travel journal of Cardinal Luigi d'Aragona's 1517 tour, on a Bosch triptych in the Brussels palace of the Counts of Nassau
suggested_refs: The Nassau Palace on the Coudenberg hill, Brussels, distinct from the Coudenberg Palace itself

stops.name: Palazzo Grimani, Venice: Bosch across the Alps
stops.date_confidence: the notes were written sporadically between 1521 and 1543, so 1521 is the start of the compilation rather than a dated sighting
stops.campa: Marcantonio Michiel, cataloguing the collections of Venice in a private notebook, records in the house of Cardinal Domenico Grimani works by the hand of Jeronimo Bosch, and describes them as canvases rather than panels. His notes were made in pieces over twenty-two years, so the year of the sighting is not fixed. Within a quarter century of the painter's death his pictures hang in a Venetian palace, on the far side of mountains he is not known to have crossed. The notebook stayed in manuscript and was not printed until 1800.
suggested_refs: Marcantonio Michiel, Notizie d'opere di disegno, compiled 1521-1543
sources: Marcantonio Michiel, Notizia d'opere di disegno

segments.name: The Name for Sale, and the Spanish Capture

stops.name: Aux Quatre Vents, Antwerp: the forged inventor
stops.date_confidence: attested. Bruegel's drawing is dated 1556 and Cock published the engraving in 1557; one lens of this research gave 1556 for the print, which is wrong by a year
stops.campa: In Antwerp the publisher Hieronymus Cock runs the print shop called Aux Quatre Vents, the House of the Four Winds, and finds that Bosch sells. Through the 1550s he issues designs by the young Pieter Bruegel in the older master's manner: the Seven Deadly Sins, the Virtues, and in 1557 an engraving after Bruegel's drawing Big Fish Eat Little Fish, published with Bosch's name on it as inventor instead of Bruegel's. The drawing is dated 1556 and the engraving 1557, forty-one years after the painter's death.
stops.quote_source: Karel van Mander, Het Schilder-boeck (Haarlem, 1604), on Bosch's compositions
suggested_refs: Hieronymus Cock's print shop Aux Quatre Vents, Antwerp, and the 1557 Big Fish Eat Little Fish engraving

stops.name: Brussels, the Duke of Alba takes the triptych
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: The Duke of Alba, sent north to break the revolt, seizes the Brussels property of William of Orange, who has fled into exile. The Garden of Earthly Delights is in it, come down to William through the Nassau inheritance. The triptych leaves the Low Countries as confiscated rebel goods, crated and shipped to Spain, and the country that made it will not have it back. In these same months Alba's tribunal is condemning men by the hundred, and the crates go south while the sentences are read.
suggested_refs: The 1568 confiscation of the Nassau collection from William of Orange

stops.name: El Escorial, the king who collected hells
stops.date_confidence: the Haywain's acquisition in 1570 and shipment to the Escorial four years later are attested; the Temptation's transfer in 1574 is inferred, since the monastery inventories do not clearly itemize it
stops.campa: Philip II buys Bosch. The Haywain enters the royal collection in 1570 and is sent up to the monastery-palace of San Lorenzo four years later; a Temptation of Saint Anthony probably goes with it, though the inventories do not clearly itemize it. The most orthodox monarch in Europe hangs hells along his own corridors and sleeps among them. A generation earlier the Spanish collector Felipe de Guevara had already written the phrase that fixed the painter for Spain, in a manuscript that stayed unprinted until 1788.
stops.quote: the inventor of monsters and chimeras
stops.quote_source: Felipe de Guevara, Comentarios de la Pintura, written c. 1560, unprinted until 1788; quoted in Walter Gibson, Hieronymus Bosch, p. 9
suggested_refs: Escorial inventory records of the Bosch acquisitions of Philip II

stops.name: El Escorial, the strawberry-tree picture given to the monks
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the auction purchase is dated 1591
stops.campa: Philip II buys The Garden of Earthly Delights at auction in 1591 and, on the eighth of July 1593, gives it to the monastery of San Lorenzo de El Escorial. The deed does not give it a title. It describes the object by its parts and by the nickname the Spanish court had fastened on it, del Madrono, the strawberry-tree picture, after the giant fruit carried across the central panel. Hieronymite monks now live with it daily, in a building where the king's own bedroom opens onto the high altar.
stops.quote: painting in oils, with two wings depicting the variety of the world, illustrated with grotesqueries by Hieronymus Bosch, known as 'Del Madroño'
stops.quote_source: Spanish royal inventory record of 8 July 1593, transferring the triptych to the monastery of El Escorial
suggested_refs: The 1593 donation record naming the triptych 'del Madrono'

stops.name: El Escorial, Siguenza defends the painting he lives with
stops.date_confidence: attested publication year; the English wording of the quotation is translator-dependent and could not be checked against the Spanish
stops.campa: Jose de Siguenza, librarian and historian of the Hieronymite order, writes a defence of the triptych hanging in his own monastery against those who call it heresy or nonsense. His argument is that the panels are painted sermons, and that what looks like indecency is the shame of mankind set out where it can be looked at. He can walk down the corridor and check the picture against the sentence. The book appears in 1605, eighty-nine years after the painter's death.
stops.quote: are a satirical comment on the shame and sinfulness of mankind
stops.quote_source: Jose de Siguenza, Historia de la Orden de San Jeronimo (1605), on The Garden of Earthly Delights; English wording translator-dependent
suggested_refs: Jose de Siguenza, Historia de la Orden de San Jeronimo (1605), book on the Escorial paintings
sources: Wikipedia, 'The Garden of Earthly Delights', citing Siguenza

stops.name: Aranjuez, the Haywain in pieces
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: The Haywain has been broken up. The Marquis of Salamanca sold off its panels separately, and in 1848 Queen Isabella II buys the central panel and has it moved to the royal palace at Aranjuez, while the wings stay behind at the Escorial. A triptych is a hinged argument: three boards that mean something only when they are opened together, hell answering paradise across the load of hay. For sixty-six years the cart hangs at Aranjuez without its hell.
suggested_refs: The dispersal of the Haywain panels by the Marquis of Salamanca and the 1848 royal purchase

stops.name: Museo del Prado, Madrid: the Haywain recomposed
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: At the Prado the scattered panels of the Haywain are formally put back together, centre and wings rejoined after most of a century apart. The object works again as it was built to work: shutters closed on a wayfarer, shutters open on the world grabbing at a cart. On the left wing the rebel angels fall out of the sky over Eden; on the right, a tower is going up in hell. The proverb behind it was Brabant speech, out of a market town where nobody wrote down who ordered the picture or why. It has hung in Madrid ever since.
suggested_refs: The 1914 recomposition of the Haywain Triptych at the Museo del Prado

stops.name: Museo del Prado, Madrid: the Garden comes down from the mountain
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: After three hundred and forty-two years at El Escorial, The Garden of Earthly Delights is brought down to Madrid and enters the Museo del Prado. It moves from a monastery, where it was seen by monks and by whoever a king let in, to a public gallery open to anybody holding a ticket. The Prado now keeps the Garden, the Haywain, the Adoration of the Magi and the Table of the Seven Deadly Sins. The four of them hang in the same building, a few rooms apart, and none of them has been in Brabant for four hundred years.
suggested_refs: Museo del Prado, room of the Bosch triptychs
sources: Museo del Prado permanent collection records

segments.name: The Sawn Triptych and the Scattered Panels

stops.name: Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga, Lisbon: the Temptation in Portuguese keeping
stops.date_confidence: attested in Portugal by at least the seventeenth century; the nominal date stands for that attestation. The mid-sixteenth-century arrival by way of Damiao de Gois is a plausible reconstruction with no document behind it
stops.campa: The Temptation of Saint Anthony triptych is in Lisbon, and has been in Portugal since at least the seventeenth century. How it got there is a genuine gap. The humanist Damiao de Gois is often proposed as the route, in the mid-1500s, and the proposal has nothing under it. What the museum hangs is the hermit besieged from every side, a village burning behind him, the pig at his feet, black masses moving in the sky; and the saint himself calm in the centre of it, two fingers raised, looking out of the panel at whoever is standing there.
suggested_refs: The Temptation of Saint Anthony triptych, Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga, Lisbon
sources: Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga provenance records

stops.name: Museum voor Schone Kunsten, Ghent: the crowded Christ
stops.date_confidence: the 1902 acquisition is attested; the attribution is not, and the panel's date is now disputed by decades
stops.campa: The Ghent museum buys a Christ Carrying the Cross in 1902: faces packed edge to edge across the whole panel, jeering mouths and rolled eyes, the Christ shut in among them with his own eyes closed. It passed for a late Bosch for a century. In October 2015 the Bosch Research and Conservation Project rejected the attribution on the evidence of the underdrawing and the framing, dated the panel well after his death and gave it to a follower. Griet Steyaert contests the finding. The picture has not changed; the label has.
stops.quote: often less pleasant than gruesome to look at
stops.quote_source: Karel van Mander, Het Schilder-boeck (Haarlem, 1604), on the effect of Bosch's paintings
suggested_refs: Christ Carrying the Cross, Museum voor Schone Kunsten Ghent, and the BRCP reattribution of October 2015
sources: Museum voor Schone Kunsten Ghent curatorial records

stops.name: Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen, Rotterdam: the Wayfarer
stops.date_confidence: no event date. The pin marks where the panel hangs now; 2016 is nominal, the year of the anniversary exhibitions
stops.campa: A small round panel hangs in Rotterdam: a ragged man with a basket on his back and one shoe off, looking over his shoulder at a broken-down house where a woman stands in the doorway and a dog snarls at his heels. It is the outside of a triptych wing, painted to be seen with the shutters shut, the picture a viewer met before anything else. The scene on the other face of this same board, Death and the Miser, is in Washington. When the triptych was sawn apart, and by whom, nobody recorded.
suggested_refs: The Wayfarer (the Pedlar) tondo, Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen, Rotterdam

stops.name: Yale University Art Gallery, New Haven: Gluttony and Lust
stops.date_confidence: no event date. The pin marks the panel's present home; 2016 is nominal
stops.campa: The Allegory of Gluttony and Lust is in New Haven, Connecticut. It was the lower half of the left wing of the same dismembered triptych, and the upper half, the Ship of Fools, is in Paris; the two have stood in one room only for the length of a loan. Whoever put the saw to the board did it to make several saleable pictures out of one object that nobody then wanted whole. What is left is a strip of oak with drinkers and bathers on it, a fat man astride a barrel, a tent pitched by the water.
suggested_refs: Allegory of Gluttony and Lust, Yale University Art Gallery

stops.name: Musee du Louvre, Paris: the Ship of Fools
stops.date_confidence: no event date. The pin marks the panel's present home; 2016 is nominal
stops.campa: The Ship of Fools is a small panel in the Louvre: a monk and a nun singing over a table set in a boat, a lute between them, a hanging fowl, a man climbing the mast with a knife, and the mast itself a living tree in leaf. Nobody in it is rowing. The whole thing is a little over half a metre high. Below this scene, on the same original board, ran the strip that is now in New Haven, and the saw went through the middle of the composition. The two halves are in different countries.
suggested_refs: Ship of Fools, Musee du Louvre, Paris

stops.name: National Gallery of Art, Washington: Death and the Miser
stops.date_confidence: no event date. The pin marks the panel's present home; 2016 is nominal
stops.campa: Death and the Miser hangs in Washington: a dying man propped in a curtained bed, a demon at the bedside holding out a sack of gold, an angel at his shoulder pointing to a crucifix in the window, and the choice unmade at the moment the picture stops. Carved into the bed frame is an owl among foliage. Specialists mine details of this kind for the proverbs that Netherlandish speech carried and painting borrowed. This is the right wing whose exterior, the Wayfarer, is in Rotterdam.
suggested_refs: Death and the Miser, National Gallery of Art, Washington DC

stops.name: Akademie der bildenden Kunste, Vienna: the unresolved Last Judgement
stops.date_confidence: the panel's own date is open: dendrochronology shows the oak was not used before 1482, giving a range of roughly 1482-1505. The pin date is nominal and marks the present location
stops.campa: A large Last Judgement triptych hangs in the Vienna academy. Dendrochronology says the oak was not worked before 1482, which leaves a range of some twenty years and no way to narrow it. Some connect the panel to the Last Judgement Philip the Handsome ordered in 1504; others hold it is a different work entirely. The donor face on the outer wing is read as Philip by one side and as nobody in particular by the other. Is this the lost commission, or is it not? Five centuries have not answered.
suggested_refs: The Last Judgement triptych, Akademie der bildenden Kunste Wien

stops.name: Gallerie dell'Accademia, Venice: the Visions of the Hereafter
stops.date_confidence: no event date. The pin marks the present holding; 2016 is nominal
stops.campa: Four narrow panels in Venice, called the Visions of the Hereafter. On one, souls are carried upward by angels through a dark tunnel toward a circle of light at the end of it, a picture that people who have never heard of Bosch recognise from other kinds of testimony. On the others, the damned go down. They descend from the Grimani collection, where Michiel saw Bosch works in the sixteenth century, and they have not left the city since. The panel with the tunnel in it is under a metre high.
suggested_refs: The Visions of the Hereafter panels, Gallerie dell'Accademia, Venice
sources: Marcantonio Michiel, Notizie d'opere di disegno

stops.name: Markt, 's-Hertogenbosch: the bronze on the square
stops.date_confidence: attested; the statue was made by August Falise in 1929 and unveiled in 1930
stops.campa: August Falise models a bronze Jeroen Bosch for the Markt, working from the portrait drawing in the Recueil d'Arras, and the town unveils it in 1930. The painter stands in the square where the workshop stood. Since 2007 a deconsecrated church a few streets off has housed the Jheronimus Bosch Art Center, which shows some sixty full-scale photographic replicas of everything he is thought to have made. The originals are in Madrid, Lisbon, Venice, Vienna, Washington, Paris, New Haven and Rotterdam.

stops.name: Germany, Fraenger turns the Garden inside out
stops.date_confidence: publication year attested; the pin is nominal, the sources giving only 'Germany' as the place
stops.campa: Wilhelm Fraenger publishes an argument that reverses the picture: the central panel is not a warning against lust but innocence recovered, painted for a heretical sect of the Free Spirit, and Bosch was their man. It is the one reading that takes the happiness of the central panel at face value instead of explaining it away. No document ties Bosch to any sect, and most Bosch scholars have rejected the thesis for eighty years. Fraenger named the sect the Homines intelligentia and gave the triptych to them outright.
stops.quote_source: Wilhelm Fraenger's name for the Adamite sect he believed commissioned the triptych, Das Tausendjahrige Reich (1947)
suggested_refs: Wilhelm Fraenger, Das Tausendjahrige Reich: Grundzuge einer Auslegung Hieronymus Boschs (1947)
sources: Wikipedia, 'The Garden of Earthly Delights', citing Fraenger

stops.name: Amsterdam, Bax reads the paintings as speech
stops.date_confidence: attested. The dissertation is Ontcijfering van Jeroen Bosch (1949); the English translation of 1979 is sometimes cited as if it were the original
stops.campa: Dirk Bax defends a dissertation at Amsterdam that decodes Bosch through Netherlandish speech: proverbs, puns, obscene idioms, sermon commonplaces, the ordinary verbal furniture of the Low Countries put into paint. A funnel on a head is a phrase. A fish in a bed is a phrase. Where Fraenger found a secret sect, Bax finds a painter speaking plainly to people who spoke his language, and unreadable afterwards only because the language moved on and the pictures did not. The dissertation is Ontcijfering van Jeroen Bosch; the English translation waits thirty years.
suggested_refs: Dirk Bax, Ontcijfering van Jeroen Bosch (1949), University of Amsterdam
sources: Dirk Bax, Ontcijfering van Jeroen Bosch (1949)

stops.name: Museo del Prado, Madrid: the readings that will not reconcile
stops.date_confidence: the pin date is von Baldass's restatement of 1960; the stop covers scholarship from Tolnay in 1937 onward, and no consensus has been reached since
stops.campa: In front of the triptych in Madrid the readings pile up and refuse to reconcile. Charles de Tolnay calls the central panel the nightmare of humanity brought on by sensual pleasure. Ludwig von Baldass restates the orthodox scheme, sin entering the world with Eve and running inexorably to hell. Erwin Panofsky argues against Fraenger and for the moralizing sense. Visitors at the rail decide for themselves whether the naked crowd in the middle is being condemned or envied. No consensus exists.
suggested_refs: Charles de Tolnay (1937), Ludwig von Baldass (1960), and the moralizing reading of the Garden
sources: Wikipedia, 'The Garden of Earthly Delights', citing De Tolnay and von Baldass

stops.name: Noordbrabants Museum, 's-Hertogenbosch: five hundred years
stops.date_confidence: the exhibition year is attested; the specific opening date of 13 February 2016 could not be confirmed from any reachable source
stops.campa: For the five hundredth anniversary of his death the Noordbrabants Museum gathers most of the surviving paintings and drawings back into the town that made them, the first time since his lifetime that they stand in one building. The Bosch Research and Conservation Project publishes its catalogue the same year: six years of technical examination, the securely autograph corpus narrowed to around twenty paintings, several long-accepted works moved to workshop and follower hands. The Prado, which lent, disputed some of the downgrades in public.
